newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks surrender gains at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks surrender gains at close.

text.p: Argentine blue-chip stocks gave back early gains to close flat Wednesday, with trade slowing to an excruciating pace hours before a debate of tax reforms in Congress, dealers said.

"We had very little volume and an overall sluggish market," said Juan Pablo Paillot of Rabello traders. "I think investors are anticipating what Congress won't do tonight, because it probably won't be able to pass all the measures."
The blue-chip MerVal index closed unchanged at 534.59, while the broad market dipped 0.2 percent in floor volume of 10.3 million pesos.
Turnover was only slightly less dismal Tuesday at 11.2 million pesos.

"When volume surged to 27 million pesos (Friday) the market had a tough act to follow," said Jose Napoli of Ignoto y Napoli brokers. "It's been unwinding ever since and I see some more downside Thursday."
The MerVal index shed 0.8 percent Tuesday after rallying 4.3 percent in the previous three sessions.
Traders said the market had started to shrug off a package of tax reforms which, after much fuss and changes, finally comes up for floor debate tonight in Congress.

"The market is discounting congressional approval sooner or later," said Napoli. "But people are reluctant to make any bets until the market consolidates at these levels and is able to take on technical resistance at around 550 on the MerVal."
The fiscal reforms have been attenuated at the committee stage although the main hike on fuel taxes remains the cornerstone of the package.
In the session over-the-counter turnover grew to 72.4 million pesos from 57.9 million Tuesday.
The broad market index inched up 0.2 percent, with winners outpacing losers 23 to 15 and 18 issues closing flat.
The best main-tier performer was oil company Sol Petroleo, which jumped 4.0 percent catching up with recent stronger gains in other sector stocks.

Holding company Garovaglio and petrochemical concern Ipako followed with gains of 1.8 percent and 1.4 percent, respectively. Garovaglio will absorb Ipako later this year under a deal announced last week.
MerVal losers were led by carmaker Ciadea, which slumped 3.3 percent, Bansud bank, off 2.2 percent, and Telecom and Telefonica, down 0.5 percent and 0.2 percent respectively.
